item.title: PM Tarique warns of anarchy as govt rolls out key pledges in Feni
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman yesterday accused unnamed political parties of trying to create “anarchy” by exploiting incidents across the country, warning that political instability would ultimately derail development and welfare programs and hurt ordinary people.
Speaking during his first visit to Feni since taking office, Tarique linked his political warning to a series of government initiatives, including Family and Farmer cards, river excavation, expansion of upazila hospitals and efforts to reopen closed industries, and urged people to remain alert to what he described as attempts to obstruct the country’s democratic process.
The prime minister made the remarks after inaugurating the first phase of the Tk1,542.16-crore Muhuri-Kahua Flood Control, Drainage and Irrigation Rehabilitation Project at Ghatghar near the Muhuri Bridge in Parshuram.
Without initially naming any party, Tarique said some political groups were capitalising on “untoward incidents” to create disorder.
He later alluded to Jamaat-e-Islami, accusing its leaders of becoming “arrogant” after winning several seats in the February 12 election and invoking the party’s role during the 1971 Liberation War.
“Leaders of a certain political party are lecturing us. I would tell them to look at their own house first,” Tarique said, before referring to allegations of violence against women and a killing involving members or leaders of the party.
The allegations were not independently substantiated in the material provided. Tarique himself said an investigation into one of the incidents was underway.
He said the government was pursuing programs ranging from Family and Farmer cards to canal excavation and expansion of healthcare, arguing that disorder would jeopardise their implementation.
“If this work is disrupted, who will suffer?” he asked. “It will be the people of this country.”
The political message came as Tarique used the daylong visit to showcase several development and social-protection initiatives in Feni, including one of the district’s largest flood-management projects.
Braving rain, he unveiled a plaque and formally launched the Muhuri-Kahua project by starting a dredger at around 2:30pm.
Approved by Ecnec on June 16, the project involves rehabilitation of 67.92 kilometres of embankments, protection of 11.73 kilometres of riverbanks, re-excavation of 83.50 kilometres of rivers and reservoirs, rehabilitation of 27 irrigation structures and construction of 77 inlets.
It is scheduled for completion by 2030.
The infrastructure was badly affected by the devastating 2024 floods, while residents of Parshuram and Fulgazi have long faced river erosion, damaged embankments, waterlogging and inadequate drainage.
Tarique said the project was part of fulfilling an election pledge and would directly benefit around 400,000 to 450,000 people.
According to the prime minister, around 34,000 hectares of farmland would receive irrigation facilities and crop production could increase by nearly 100,000 tons after implementation.
He said increased agricultural production would help farmers earn more while contributing to efforts to keep food prices within consumers’ purchasing power.
Tarique also highlighted measures his government has taken since assuming office, presenting them as fulfilment of election commitments.
He referred to the waiver of agricultural loans of up to Tk10,000 for small farmers.
The prime minister also highlighted the Family Card program, saying the government intended eventually to provide the benefit to mothers in eligible families across rural and urban Bangladesh.
The program was formally launched nationally in March, initially reaching 37,567 women, and the government has since been working on its phased expansion.
During yesterday’s Feni visit, Tarique attended a program involving Family and Farmer cards as well as honorariums for people serving at religious institutions.
Healthcare also featured prominently in the prime minister’s speech.
Tarique said his government planned to upgrade upazila-level hospitals from 50 to 150 beds over the next five years, with expanded services including dialysis and maternal and child healthcare.
His Feni visit also included a tree-planting program at Begum Khaleda Zia Women’s College in Fulgazi and the inauguration of electricity supply to the national grid from rooftop solar systems installed on government buildings.
The solar installations across Fulgazi, Parshuram and Chhagalnaiya have a combined capacity of around 962 kilowatts.
Thousands of people gathered along the Muhuri River and roads in Parshuram to see the prime minister during the visit.
Feni carries particular political and family significance for Tarique. His maternal grandfather, Eskandar Majumder, hailed from Fulgazi, while his mother, former prime minister Khaleda Zia, was elected to Parliament several times from Feni-1.

item.title: DSCC administrator: Hawkers outside designated areas to face action
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation ( DSCC ) Administrator Md Abdus Salam has warned that goods of hawkers occupying roads and footpaths outside designated areas will be confiscated and legal action taken against them.
He said no hawker would be allowed to operate anywhere in Dhaka except at locations designated and approved by the city corporation.
The DSCC administrator made the remarks while speaking to journalists on Thursday after inspecting cleanliness, illegal encroachments and public sufferings in the Dhalpur area of the capital.
“We have designated certain footpaths and places for hawkers . Outside these areas , strict action will be taken if hawkers illegally occupy any footpath, including the main road from Zero Point to Sadarghat,” he said.
Salam said all hawkers in the city would have to come under a regulated system and register with the city corporation.
“No hawker will be allowed to operate anywhere in Dhaka without registration,” he said.
Regarding hawkers returning to footpaths after eviction drives, the administrator said authorities would now confiscate their goods and file cases against them alongside eviction.
On whether hawkers would be served notices before eviction and whether they would be rehabilitated, Salam said the government had already held several meetings with hawker leaders before taking the decision.
DSCC Administrator Md Abdus Salam inspects cleanliness and illegal encroachments in Dhalpur, Dhaka, on Thursday, October 1, 2026. Photo: Courtesy
“So, there is no question of issuing new notices,” he said.
Regarding rehabilitation, the DSCC administrator urged journalists to consider whether residents who pay taxes to the city corporation want hawkers to be rehabilitated on roads and footpaths.
During the inspection, Salam also expressed dissatisfaction over public suffering caused by prolonged Dhaka Water Supply and Sewerage Authority (Wasa) works at the entrance to DSCC Regional Office-5.
He said thousands of people visiting the office every day were suffering because of the ongoing Wasa work.
He said WASA and other service agencies had been instructed to complete road excavation and related works in a coordinated manner within the stipulated timeframe.
For a permanent solution to such problems, Salam said regular meetings were being held every 15 days under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to improve coordination among service agencies.
He said the DSCC was working in coordination with Wasa, the city corporation, T&T, the power sector and other relevant agencies to resolve the longstanding problems.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,110 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Thursday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,110.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified both of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,009, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 101, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
The two new suspected fatalities were reported across Sylhet and Chittagong divisions, with one death each recorded in Habiganj district and Chittagong district.
A total of 1,132 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Thursday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 192,863.
During the same period, 82 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 21,602.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 170,877 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 163,973 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Muktadir: Overlapping projects across ministries hinder productivity
item.description:
Industries Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir on Thursday said eliminating overlapping projects run by different ministries could ensure double-digit efficiency gains as the government moves to review such duplication to boost national productivity.
Speaking at an event organised by the Ministry of Industries in Motijheel, he said efforts are underway to examine whether projects implemented by different ministries overlap.
“No issue today is confined to one country; we have to look at the whole world,” the minister said, adding that it is not possible to remain outside the existing global system even if one wishes to.
“So, there is no alternative to raising productivity. The nation that increases productivity will be the one that advances,” he said.
Pointing to the ready-made garment (RMG) sector, Muktadir said it has demonstrated how progress can be achieved even with workers from marginalised sections of society.
Speaking at the event, Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) Executive Director Nazneen Ahmed said small enterprises need support to grow into medium-sized ones, and that the government coordinates with various sectors to facilitate such growth.
She stressed the need to examine whether these initiatives involve duplication.
Nazneen said the government needs assistance in designing productivity training, adding that replacing people with machines should not be the goal.
Instead, she said, attention should be given to how machinery and technology can enhance workers’ skills, while innovation also needs to be increased.
The CPD executive director noted that women’s participation in large industries is declining.
“Women cannot take the skills training required for automation because of household pressures, so they are falling behind in skill-based jobs,” she said.
She also proposed a refinancing scheme for the SME sector, saying linking loans to productivity improvement could lead to significant growth in the sector.

item.title: PM opens Tk1,542cr flood control, drainage, irrigation project in Feni
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday inaugurated the Tk1,542.16-crore Muhuri-Kohua Flood Control, Drainage and Irrigation Project rehabilitation (Phase I) at Feni aiming to strengthen flood protection, drainage and irrigation facilities in the district.
The prime minister inaugurated the project at around 2.17 pm on Thursday at the Kheyaghat Ghat-Muhuri Bridge area in Parshuram upazila and later exchanged greetings with local people at the venue.
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) approved the project on June 16 at an estimated cost of Tk1,542.16 crore.
Under the project, 67.92 kilometers of flood-control embankments will be rehabilitated, 11.73 kilometers of riverbanks protected and 83.50 kilometers of rivers and water bodies re-excavated.
Besides, 27 irrigation structures will be rehabilitated and 77 inlets will be constructed under the project, which is scheduled to be completed by 2030.
In its next phase, there are plans to construct new embankments along the Muhuri and Kohua rivers and undertake embankment construction, excavation and rehabilitation works along the Silonia River.
Environment, Forest and Climate change Minister and Feni-3 Lawmaker Abdul Awal Mintoo, Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee, State Minister for Water Resources Forhad Hossain Azad, Feni-1 Lawmaker Munshi Rafiqul Alam, Feni-2 Lwmaker Joynal Abdin, Lawmaker Rahana Akter Ranu, among other, were present on the occasion.
Earlier, the prime minister arrived in Feni at around 1:15pm on his daylong tour to attend a series of programs.
After inaugurating the Muhuri-Kohua project in Parshuram, he is scheduled to travel to Fulgazi, where he will join a tree-planting program at Begum Khaleda Zia Women’s College.
He will later visit the Fulgazi District Council Dak Bungalow, where he will inaugurate the supply of electricity to the national grid from the rooftop solar power system installed at the facility.
The prime minister will then rest and offer prayers at the Dak Bungalow. Later in the afternoon, he will attend a program at Fulgazi Government Pilot High School ground, where he will distribute Family Cards and Farmer Cards and provide honorariums to mosque imams, muezzins, khadims and priests.
He is also scheduled to address a public gathering at the venue before returning to Dhaka in the evening.
Under a government initiative, solar systems with a combined capacity of 962.5 kilowatts have been installed on government buildings in Fulgazi, Parshuram and Chhagalnaiya upazilas, including 415 kilowatts in Chhagalnaiya, 298 kilowatts in Parshuram and 249 kilowatts in Fulgazi.
A total of 510 people in Fulgazi are set to receive Family Cards, while 7,643 people across Feni district will receive Farmer Cards.
Honorariums will also be provided to 238 imams, muezzins, khadims and priests in Fulgazi.
Tarique Rahman’s maternal grandfather Easkandar Majumder’s ancestral home is in Sreepur village of Fulgazi upazila in Feni.
Feni-1 constituency also has a longstanding association with his mother, former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia, who was elected from the constituency several times since 1991.

item.title: Mandatory BIN: Small entrepreneurs trapped in red tape
item.description:
A new requirement mandating a business identification number (BIN) to open business bank accounts and secure expansion loans has hit cottage, micro, small, and medium enterprises (CMSMEs) hard.
Effective from the current fiscal year, the rule has created significant operational hurdles for small business owners who lack a BIN, restricting their access to routine banking services and credit.
According to data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS), Bangladesh is home to roughly 11.7 million economic units, nearly 99% of which belong to the micro, cottage, small, and medium category.
Employing over 30 million people, the sector accounts for nearly 85% of industrial employment and contributes 25% to 32% to the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
Acknowledging the hardship faced by small business owners, the Association of Bankers, Bangladesh (ABB) has formally urged the National Revenue Board (NBR) to relax or withdraw the rule.
In a letter sent to the NBR chairman, the ABB highlighted that many small-scale entrepreneurs do not yet possess a BIN and face lengthy delays trying to gather the required paperwork to register.
Consequently, their daily business operations and credit access are severely disrupted.
The ABB proposed exempting micro, cottage, and small businesses from the mandatory BIN requirement.
Alternatively, the association requested a phased implementation approach to allow entrepreneurs additional time to prepare, along with allowing banks to accept existing institutional documents as supporting proof.
However, the NBR stated that it cannot grant the ABB's request.
Revenue officials clarified that the condition is a statutory mandate embedded in the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012. Under Sections 4(3)(a) and (b) of the Act, presenting a BIN is legally compulsory for opening or operating current and short-term deposit (STD) accounts, as well as obtaining loans from banks or financial institutions.
A senior NBR official, requesting anonymity, noted that the law applies universally across all business sizes to bring informal activities into the formal economy and expand the tax and VAT net.
Thus, neither banks nor the NBR possess the authority to waive the rule administratively.
Entrepreneurs clarify that their objection lies not in the objective of the regulation, but in its execution.
Shah Poran, a small business owner at Bangshal, pointed out that while applying for a BIN online is straightforward, gathering the prerequisite documentation poses a major challenge.
The complex paperwork and additional expenses often lead to bureaucratic delays and harassment.
He suggested that implementing the law in phases rather than enforcing a sudden blanket mandate would ease the transition for small businesses.
While making BIN mandatory aims to widen the VAT net, industry stakeholders emphasize the need to balance revenue collection with safeguarding the growth and financial inclusion of small enterprises.

item.title: FY26 VAT collection: 85% LTUs fail to meet target
item.description:
Around 85% of large corporate taxpayers, including cigarette, cement, gas, and mobile-phone companies, failed to meet the government's value-added tax (VAT) targets last FY26 amid sluggish business environment and lower-than-expected consumption.
Of the 34 business sectors under the VAT Large Taxpayers Unit (VAT-LTU), 29 missed their respective targets, according to the latest provisional compiled data of the National Board of Revenue (NBR).
Officials said the targets were apparently set without adequately considering the prevailing economic and business conditions.
The VAT-LTU had set a revenue collection target of Tk108,000 crore for FY26, against which it collected Tk87,500 crore, although collection grew by nearly 10% year on year.
Cigarette companies missed their target by 17%, or Tk8,856 crore, despite recording nearly 19% year-on-year growth in VAT payments.
VAT collection from five gas companies fell short of the target by 37.70% and declined by nearly 2% year on year.
The five gas companies paid Tk218 crore less in VAT in FY26 than in the previous fiscal year.
Similarly, the VAT-LTU collected Tk1,236 crore less from 17 private commercial banks than their combined target.
However, collection from the banks increased slightly, by nearly 3% year on year.
The VAT-LTU collected Tk76,953 crore in FY25, compared with Tk73,660 crore in FY24.
VAT collection from large taxpayers fell short of the target by Tk8,337 crore in FY25, while the shortfall increased sharply to Tk24,538 crore in FY26.
In FY25, VAT collection from 25 of the 34 sectors under the LTU recorded positive year-on-year growth.
In FY26, however, 20 sectors registered positive growth, while the remaining sectors recorded negative growth.
The number of sectors witnessing a decline in VAT collection increased to 14 in FY26 from nine in FY25.
Mobile phone, cement, paper, footwear, packaging materials, electrical goods, coconut oil, BTRC, oxygen, telecom equipment, and manufacturers were among the sectors that recorded negative growth in VAT collection last year.
Despite the slowdown across a majority of sectors, the LTU-VAT receipts grew by nearly 10% in FY26, which was 4% in FY25.

item.title: BRUR expels 11, including 3 teachers, over Shaheed Abu Sayed killing
item.description:
Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur (BRUR) has permanently expelled 11 individuals, including three faculty members and eight officials and staff, over their involvement in the killing of student Abu Sayed during the 2024 Anti-Discrimination Student Movement.
The punitive measure was approved during the 123rd meeting of the BRUR Syndicate, the university’s highest policy-making body, on Wednesday night, Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Md Showkat Ali confirmed on Thursday afternoon.
The three permanently expelled faculty members are Mashiur Rahman, former associate professor of the Mathematics Department; Asaduzzaman Mandal alias Asad, associate professor of Public Administration; and Shariful Islam, associate professor of Political Science and former proctor.
The expelled employees include former Assistant Registrar Rafiul Hasan Russel, Assistant Registrar Hafijur Rahman alias Tufan, Section Officer Moniruzzaman Palash, Office Assistant-cum-Computer Operator Mahabubar Rahman alias Babu, Security Guard Nur Alam Mia, and MLSS staff members Mohammad Nurunnabi Mandal and AKM Amir Hossain, alongside an 11th individual confirmed by university administration.
BRUR Registrar Prof Dr Md Ferdous Rahman said administrative procedures are underway to execute the Syndicate's order. Terming Abu Sayed’s death a momentous and painful chapter in the university's history, VC Prof. Shawkat Ali reaffirmed that disciplinary actions were taken strictly in accordance with university statutes following an internal probe.
Abu Sayed, a key coordinator of the quota reform movement and a student of the English Department, was shot dead by police on July 16, 2024, near the university's main gate. Footage of Sayed standing unarmed with outstretched arms, facing police gunfire, went viral, sparking nationwide protests that ultimately led to the fall of the Sheikh Hasina-led government.

item.title: Minister: 4.34 lakh Bangladeshis got overseas jobs in seven months
item.description:
Expatriate Welfare Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury on Thursday said that around 434,000 Bangladeshi workers have got overseas employment abroad over the past seven months despite ongoing wars.
“The government hopes to do even better and keep its place in the global labor market under difficult circumstances,” he said while inaugurating a trolley service designed to facilitate the convenient transport of luggage for expatriate workers and inspecting the Expatriate Welfare Desk inside Chittagong's Shah Amanat International Airport.
During the visit, the Minister spoke directly with outbound passengers and asked about their needs, the facilities available to them, and the problems they face. He stressed that workers going abroad must be skilled. Sending more workers without proper skills, he said, would bring no real benefit to the country.
Speaking to airport authorities about passenger healthcare, he directed them to set up an emergency medical center for expatriate workers quickly. Instructions to select a site have already been given. He added that the government is fully prepared to provide all necessary facilities for expatriate workers.
He also pointed to the hardship caused by long waits at the airport, especially when flights are delayed or rescheduled. The government plans to build a rest house near the airport so passengers can stay comfortably, whatever the situation, he added.

item.title: France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
item.description:
Security forces in France on Wednesday detained over 600 people as protests at high schools in parts of the country have intensified.
Authorities said violent clashes and arson attacks have also left dozens of security personnel wounded.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez condemned what he called an “escalation of violence” outside certain schools.
The violence left 83 police officers and gendarmes wounded on Wednesday, he said, adding that 32 teachers and pupils were also injured. The protests affected 356 schools, the minister noted.
He slammed the “targeting of law enforcement officers, the throwing of projectiles, acts of violence, verbal abuse, attempted arson, and what amounts... to urban violence.”
Teenagers at French lycées (equivalent to US high schools) have been blockading their schools since last week.
They are protesting overcrowded classes, heavy workloads, poor-quality learning materials and teacher shortages.
“There are cockroaches and rats everywhere in the school,” Fadila, a 17-year-old student, told the Reuters news agency. She said temperatures in classrooms could swing from sweltering to below freezing, depending on the weather.
The movement began in the Ile-de-France region around the capital, Paris, but has since spread to other regions.
The cities worst affected Wednesday include Paris, Bordeaux in the southwest and Lyon in the southeast, and the northern city of Lille, where police again used tear gas in clashes, the AFP news agency reported.
President Emmanuel Macron said the young people’s concerns were legitimate but could in no way justify violence and attacks on police officers and teachers, among others.
“High schools are meant to be open and to share knowledge. They are not meant to be blockaded or to have trash ⁠cans set on fire,” he told reporters in Madrid.
Both Macron and Nunez accused far-left groups of inciting violence during the protests.
“We observed that, in certain places, ⁠there were ​individuals acting as agitators — people who, moreover, moved from one school to another to stir ​up high school and other students and incite them to commit acts of violence,” Nunez said.
Over the past few days, officials and politicians have denounced the left-wing La France Insoumise (France Unbowed or LFI) party and its presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon for rhetoric they said was stoking students’ anger.
On Monday, Melenchon had accused the government of implementing a “crackdown” with “obvious racist undertones.”
“Hands off our youth!” he wrote on social media, while encouraging LFI activists and officials to support the protests wherever they could.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu called the accusation of racism “an insult” and accused Melenchon of “racializing a debate about student security and adding to division where a responsible politician should be looking to restore calm.”

item.title: UN says strikes on Afghanistan kill 10 civilians
item.description:
The United Nations said airstrikes on Thursday killed at least 10 civilians in Afghanistan, mostly children, after Pakistan said it targeted militants.
Afghanistan and Pakistan went to war earlier this year and, with no permanent resolution reached on security issues, there have been sporadic attacks since a March truce.
The latest strikes hit Helmand province as well as Kunar, which borders Pakistan, the UN mission in Afghanistan said.
“At least 10 civilians were killed, most of them children, and nine people injured,” Unama said in a statement, confirming a toll previously given by Afghan officials.
Islamabad confirmed “planned and calibrated” strikes in Afghanistan, without detailing locations, which it said targeted militants.
Two Helmand residents told AFP that three airstrikes hit their village.
Pakistan’s information ministry said two locations in Afghanistan were hit “based on credible intelligence, selective targeting of terrorist camps and hideouts.”
Alongside neighboring Kandahar province, which was hit by an airstrike last week, Helmand in southern Afghanistan holds great importance for the Taliban movement.
Speaking by phone from Helmand’s Safar village, 50-year-old resident Abdul Wahid said the strikes killed four people and wounded seven.
Another villager, Qudrat Ullah, said he was home when his neighbors’ house was hit.
“The whole area is destroyed,” the 32-year-old said, adding that residents were being kept away from the strike sites.
“There were civilians, children, women; they have killed them. There is no military or anything else,” he told AFP by phone.
Two children were admitted to a hospital in Helmand’s provincial capital Lashkar Gah run by Italian NGO EMERGENCY, the organization told AFP.
Pakistan’s information ministry reported an initial toll of 22 militants killed, and weapons and ammunition destroyed.
Islamabad accuses Afghanistan of harboring militants behind frequent bomb and gun attacks in Pakistan, which have killed both civilians and security personnel.
The Taliban government denies this and criticizes Pakistan for violating Afghanistan’s sovereignty and killing civilians.
In mountainous Kunar province, an AFP journalist saw the remains of stone houses in the remote Chugam Valley.
Mohammad Hashim, a farmer, said he rushed to rescue residents after the pre-dawn attack.
“There was a woman, she was screaming for help to get her out of the rubble. She was having trouble breathing and told us that there are more people over there,” the 30-year-old told AFP.
“We went there to dig, and there was a man with four children who were killed,” he added.
The latest strikes follow bombardment last week on multiple Afghan provinces, which the Taliban government said killed multiple civilians. Pakistan said it targeted militants.
More than 500 civilians have been killed in violence between the two countries since October, according to figures from the United Nations mission in Afghanistan.

item.title: Dengue: Four more die as 1,978 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Four people have died of dengue across Bangladesh in the last 24 hours, while 1,978 were hospitalized during the same period, according to a statement issued by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Thursday.
According to DGHS data, 249 people have died of dengue in the country so far this year, including 148 deaths recorded in September alone.
A total of 81,598 people have been hospitalized with dengue this year.
In the last 24 hours, 2 people died in Rajshahi Division, while 1 each died in the Dhaka North City Corporation area and Mymensingh Division.

item.title: BNP draws the line as Misty forced to quit
item.description:
The BNP’s widening disciplinary drive has reached Parliament, with reserved-seat lawmaker Ferdousi Ahmed Misty resigning on Thursday on Prime Minister and party Chairman Tarique Rahman’s instruction amid allegations surrounding the attack, looting and demolition of the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur.
Her resignation, coming just a day after the BNP dissolved its entire Dhaka North City committee and announced disciplinary action against 14 leaders and activists of the party and its affiliated organisations, marks the highest-profile action yet as the ruling party seeks to rein in alleged extortion, land grabbing, violence and other activities carried out using its political identity.
Misty, who entered Parliament only five months ago, submitted her resignation to Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed on Thursday afternoon.
Her Women’s Seat-23 became vacant immediately upon receipt of the letter under Article 67(2) of the Constitution, the Speaker said.
The move followed a directive from Tarique after allegations emerged linking Misty to the September 24 attack on Radda, a longstanding maternal and child healthcare facility in Mirpur-1.
Misty has denied involvement and the allegations against her remain under investigation.
The action against a sitting ruling-party MP significantly raises the stakes of a disciplinary campaign that BNP leaders say will target anyone who uses the party’s name as cover for criminal or unethical activities.
It also comes as the government and BNP face growing scrutiny over allegations of land grabbing, extortion and violence involving ruling-party leaders and activists at different levels.
The scale of the latest disciplinary action became apparent on Wednesday.
The BNP dissolved its 51-member Dhaka North City convening committee, headed by convener Aminul Haque and member secretary Mostafa Zaman, saying a new committee would be announced soon.
No reason was given for dissolving the committee.
Three Dhaka North BNP leaders, Shah Ali thana joint convener Khalil Chowdhury, C-Block unit general secretary Anwar Hossain and city unit member Hafizur Rahman Shukku, were expelled from all party positions, including primary membership, over alleged “immoral and anti-organisational activities”.
The Dhaka North Jubo Dal and Dhaka West Chhatra Dal committees were also dissolved, officially because their terms had expired.
Five Chhatra Dal leaders and several activists and leaders associated with Jubo Dal, Swechchhasebak Dal and Sramik Dal also faced disciplinary action, taking the number expelled to 14.
The party announcements did not formally link those decisions to the Radda attack.
But the measures came as allegations of involvement by local BNP figures in the attack were under scrutiny, and less than 24 hours later the disciplinary action reached one of the party’s own MPs.
The Radda MCH-FP Centre was attacked late on September 24.
A large group allegedly entered the premises, held security guards hostage and vandalised and looted the facility. Parts of the centre were subsequently demolished using heavy machinery.
The attack triggered widespread criticism, particularly because the centre had provided maternal and child healthcare to low-income residents of Mirpur for decades.
As investigations began, the names of several local political figures surfaced.
Questions were also raised about Misty’s previous association with a cooperative that had sought allocation of the land on which the Radda centre stands.
Documents cited in media reports showed that Misty had served as president of the cooperative while she was a Ward 8 councillor, and her name and signature appeared on an application seeking allocation of the land.
A signboard bearing the cooperative’s name was subsequently found at the Radda site.
Misty acknowledged her past association with the organisation but said she no longer had any involvement with it. She has consistently denied involvement in the attack, vandalism or attempted takeover of Radda.
The government has also stopped short of declaring her responsible.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said legal action would follow if investigators found evidence of anyone’s involvement, stressing that allegations had to be established before responsibility could be determined.
Despite the unresolved investigation, the political consequences came swiftly.
Tarique directed Misty to relinquish her parliamentary seat, according to the prime minister’s press secretary.
Misty went to the National Parliament on Thursday and submitted her resignation directly to the speaker.
She avoided explaining the decision in detail while leaving Parliament, telling reporters that she would abide by whatever decision the BNP took.
The speaker later confirmed that the resignation had taken effect immediately.
“Under the constitutional provisions, her seat became vacant as soon as we received the letter,” Hafiz said, adding that the relevant documents would be forwarded to the Election Commission.
The Parliament Secretariat subsequently formally declared Women’s Seat-23 vacant from October 1.
Misty had barely begun her parliamentary career. She was among the BNP-alliance candidates elected to the reserved women’s seats this year and took oath on May 3.
BNP leaders have sought to frame the broader disciplinary campaign as a warning that political identity will not provide protection to anyone involved in extortion, land grabbing, violence or other criminal activities.
Party leaders have said allegations should first be investigated, but action would follow where wrongdoing is established.
That distinction remains important in Misty’s case: her resignation is a political and organizational consequence, not a finding of criminal responsibility.
Whether the tougher approach produces a wider change will depend on whether it is applied consistently beyond the high-profile Radda controversy and against politically influential figures elsewhere.
For now, however, the message from the BNP leadership has moved beyond warnings and expulsions at the grassroots.
With Misty’s resignation, it has cost a ruling-party lawmaker her seat in Parliament.

item.title: CCGP approves procurement worth Tk70,000cr for MRT projects
item.description:
The Cabinet Committee on Government Purchase (CCGP) on Thursday recommended approval of procurement proposals involving Tk68,586.14 crore for several packages under the Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Development projects, including MRT Line-1 and MRT Line-5 Northern Route.
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury presided over the meeting held at Bangladesh Secretariat.
The proposals, placed by the Road Transport and Highways Division, cover civil works, main lines and stations, track and electrical facilities, signalling and telecommunication systems and depot construction under projects jointly financed by the Bangladesh government and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).
For MRT Line-1, the committee recommended procurement approval for six packages.
The CP-02 package for civil and building works at the depot has a contract value of Tk4,285.07 crore, with SINOHYDRO-SEBCL JV as the recommended bidder.
The CP-06 package for construction of the main line and stations from north of Nadda Station to Airport Station, covering 5.182 km, has a contract value of Tk11,590.58 crore. NISHIMATSU-TPL-TODA JV of Japan has been recommended for the package.
The CP-09 package for track works and electrical facilities has a contract value of Tk11,065.58 crore, with L&T-Sumitomo Consortium (LTSC) recommended as the bidder.
The CP-10 package covering the signal system, telecommunication system, platform screen doors and Enterprise Resource Management System has a contract value of Tk6,446.65 crore. Larsen and Toubro Limited of India has been recommended for the package.
The committee also recommended approval of the CP-04 package for construction of the main line and stations from north of Rampura Station to Natun Bazar Station. The package has a contract value of Tk18,037.26 crore, with TOKYU-MIL (MAX Infrastructure Ltd.) Joint Venture of Japan recommended as the bidder.
Another MRT Line-1 package, CP-07, involving construction of the main line and stations from the transition point to the start of the Balu River over 5.007km, has a contract value of Tk2,534.09 crore. CREC-MIL-MBEC Joint Venture has been recommended for the package.
For the MRT Line-5 Northern Route, the committee recommended approval of two procurement proposals.
The CP-03 package for construction of the main line and five stations on the elevated section from Hemayetpur Station to Amin Bazar Transition and from Natun Bazar Transition to Vatara Station has a contract value of Tk2,670.99 crore. CREC-MIL-MBEC Joint Venture has been recommended as the bidder.
The CP-02 package for construction of civil and building works at the depot has a contract value of Tk1,847.52 crore, with CPC-HANIL Joint Venture recommended for the work.
The total value of the eight packages is about Tk68,477.74 crore, based on the contract values provided in the proposals.
The CCGP recommended approval of all the proposals.

item.title: Disciplinary action against 2 Biman officials over Zamzam water delay
item.description:
Disciplinary action has been taken against two Biman Bangladesh Airlines officials over a delay in delivering Zamzam water to passengers on a flight that arrived in Dhaka from Medina after an Umrah pilgrimage.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines General Manager Mohiuddin Ahmed, also serving as the public relations chief, confirmed the matter to the media on Thursday night.
The incident occurred after Biman flight BG338 landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 9:10am on Thursday.
The Zamzam water allocated for Umrah passengers on the flight was not delivered to the baggage belt on time.
According to a Biman press release, a preliminary investigation found that negligence in container offloading and operational handling caused the delay.
Biman took departmental action against Baggage In-charge Monirul Islam Pradhan and Flight Supervisor Saddam Hossain over negligence of duty.
The airline said that after learning about the delay, it immediately arranged Zamzam water from its reserved stock and distributed it among the Umrah pilgrims.
The other container was later located and delivered, it said.
Biman said it has strengthened internal monitoring to prevent similar incidents in the future and remains committed to providing uninterrupted service to passengers.

item.title: BTRC proposal to give officials 60pc allowance on basic pay raises questions
item.description:
The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) has decided to provide its officials and employees with a ‘regulatory allowance’ at the rate of 60 per cent of their basic salary every month.

In support of the allowance, commission officials cite their long-standing role in collecting government revenue, their responsibilities in regulating the telecommunications sector, and the restriction preventing them from joining any other technology company for six months after leaving their jobs. At its latest commission meeting, the BTRC also decided to send a proposal to the government on the matter.

However, public administration experts raised questioned on the justification for providing the allowance at 60 per cent of basic salary. They say the justification for a special allowance for officials and employees of a regulatory body cannot be determined solely by the amount of revenue it collects.

Former secretary and former rector of the Bangladesh Public Administration Training Centre (BPATC) AKM Abdul Awal Majumder does not support the BTRC officials’ justification for receiving a 60 per cent regulatory allowance.

Asked about the matter, he told Prothom Alo, “Collecting revenue from the telecommunications sector is part of BTRC’s job. That is what they joined the organisation to do. So it is not reasonable to demand something extra on the grounds of collecting more revenue.”

Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) was established in 2002 as the regulatory body for the country’s telecommunications sector. It was established under the Bangladesh Telecommunication Act, 2001. Its main responsibilities are to ensure the orderly development of the country’s telecommunications system, ensure service quality and establish effective regulation of the sector.

BTRC’s responsibilities include issuing licences for telecommunications services, spectrum management, overseeing service quality and pricing, protecting consumer interests, ensuring compliance with licence conditions and regulating the activities of various entities in the telecommunications sector.

Alongside its regulatory functions, the commission collects licence fees, renewal fees, revenue-sharing payments and spectrum charges from licensed telecommunications companies.

However, BTRC has placed revenue collection at the centre of its justification for the allowance. According to data from the commission’s finance, accounts and revenue department, BTRC collected a total of Tk 857.80 billion (85,779.82 crore) in revenue over 25 years, from the 2001-02 to 2025-26 fiscal years. In the latest 2025-26 fiscal year, revenue collection stood at Tk 38.85 billion (3,885.24 crore).

The government also sets revenue collection targets for BTRC as part of its revenue estimates. Those targets are being increased year after year. For example, in the budget concerning revenue earnings of the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology, BTRC’s revenue target has been set at Tk 60.36 billion (6,036 crore) for the 2026-27 fiscal year. It has been raised to Tk 66.40 billion (6,640 crore) for 2027-28 and Tk 73.04 billion (7,304 crore) for 2028-29.

However, BTRC is not operated as a commercial entity. The commission is responsible for collecting the revenue that the government receives from various licensed telecommunications companies. Most of that money is deposited into the government treasury.

Questions over outstanding dues

Experts said that although BTRC collects a large amount of revenue, the performance of the commission as a regulator cannot be assessed solely by the amount of revenue it collects. The quality of telecommunications services, consumer complaints, operators’ compliance with licence conditions, spectrum management and protection of consumer interests are also part of its responsibilities.

Questions have also been raised recently over a large amount of money owed to the government by the telecommunications sector. In information provided to parliament in June this year, Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam said the country’s four mobile operators owed the government a total of Tk 131.44 billion (13,144 crore) in revenue.

Of this, Grameenphone owed Tk 61.02 billion (6,101.82 crore), Teletalk Tk 59.54 billion (5,954 crore), Robi Tk 6.15 billion (615 crore) and Banglalink Tk 4.73 billion (473 crore). The outstanding amounts include licence fees, revenue-sharing payments, spectrum fees, administrative fines and audit objections, among other items.

BTRC has also been unable to collect long-standing dues owed by International Internet Gateway (IIG) operators. According to BTRC data, the government has around Tk e billion (200 crore) in outstanding dues from 24 IIG companies.

Collecting these large outstanding amounts, ensuring service quality and enforcing compliance with licence conditions are also part of BTRC’s responsibilities as a regulatory body. The commission’s performance in these areas has been questioned at various times.

Justification for a 60 pc allowance

In its documents, BTRC cited not only revenue collection but also the nature of the officials’ responsibilities and their professional expertise in proposing a special allowance for its officers and employees.

The document said BTRC officers and employees are responsible for establishing, operating and regulating telecommunications services, ensuring service quality, collecting revenue and depositing money into the government treasury. Incentives are needed to maintain their efficiency, professionalism and impartiality. For this reason, a regulatory allowance at the rate of 60 per cent of basic salary has been proposed for the commission’s officers and employees.

In this regard, BTRC also cited benefits available to officials of several other government institutions. The document mentions incentive bonuses equivalent to basic salaries for officials of Bangladesh Bank and Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC), and a risk allowance of 20 per cent for officials of the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC).

Meanwhile, under the amended provisions of the Telecommunications Act, no BTRC commissioner, employee or consultant may join any licensed telecommunications company for at least six months after leaving the job.

Such provisions are generally intended to reduce potential conflicts of interest arising when someone leaves a regulatory body and quickly joins an organisation subject to its regulation.

The BTRC document highlighted this post-employment restriction as one of the reasons for providing financial incentives to its officers and employees.

Asked about the matter, BTRC Chairman Major General (retd) Md Emdad Ul Bari told Prothom Alo that compensation for BTRC officials should be considered because, as regulators of the telecommunications sector, they have no opportunity to work in the sector for at least six months after leaving their jobs.

According to him, the telecommunications sector changes rapidly every day. As a result, if an official remains outside the sector for six months, there is a risk that their professional skills and experience will quickly become outdated.

He said the proposal for the regulatory allowance was made after considering the incentives available at other government institutions and the BTRC’s revenue collection opportunities.

Source of the money

BTRC officials say that to maintain discipline in the telecommunications sector, the commission also collects money outside the amounts specified in its guidelines, such as share transfer fees, merger fees and administrative fines. According to commission data, more than Tk 12.15 billion (1,215 crore0 was collected from these sources over 21 years, from 2005 to 2026.

On the other hand, according to BTRC documents, the commission spends approximately Tk 2.45 crore a month on salaries and allowances for its officers and employees. Over 21 years, the expenditure amounts to around Tk 617 crore.

A senior BTRC official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Prothom Alo that the government could use a portion of the money collected by the commission from various sources to provide the regulatory allowance.

item.title: Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman arrested in case over airport disorder and assault on official
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has arrested former army major Akhtaruzzaman. He was arrested from his home in DOHS (Defence Officers’ Housing Society), Cantonment, in the capital on Friday afternoon.

DMP Additional Commissioner (DB) Mohammad Shafiqul Islam confirmed the arrest to Prothom Alo, saying Akhtaruzzaman had been taken to the DB office.

He further said that a lawsuit was lodged against him at Airport police station on Thursday night over allegations of creating disorder at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport amid a shortage of luggage trolleys, obstructing government officials in the discharge of their duties, and assaulting an on-duty security official.

He was arrested in connection with that case today, Mohammad Shafiqul Islam added.

The case against retired Major Akhtaruzzaman includes allegations of obstructing government duties, causing injury, using criminal force, intentional insult and issuing threats.

Quoting the case statement, the police said that a shortage of trolleys occurred around the No. 8 luggage belt shortly after passengers disembarked from a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight (BG-338) arriving from Madinah, Saudi Arabia, at around 10.45 am on Thursday. Delays in collecting luggage led to frustration and tension among passengers.

At the request of Dhaka-5 MP Mohammad Kamal Hossain, Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad went to the scene to assess the situation.

Police said that while Ragib Samad was attempting to calm the situation, retired Major Akhtaruzzaman approached him in an aggressive manner. He allegedly threatened the airport executive director publicly, saying, “I’ll beat you up” and “I’ll drag you out by the neck.” He also allegedly made offensive remarks about the Minister for Civil Aviation and Tourism.

The case statement further alleges that protocol assistants accompanying Akhtaruzzaman began recording video on their mobile phones inside the airport’s restricted KPI area. Security supervisor Warrant Officer Mohammad Kamal Uddin, who was on duty there, asked them to stop recording. Akhtaruzzaman allegedly became angry, verbally abused the officer and subsequently assaulted him.

The case also includes allegations that bottles of holy Zamzam water collected by passengers were damaged and that Akhtaruzzaman behaved aggressively towards a representative of Biman Bangladesh Airlines.

Police officials involved in the investigation said they would collect CCTV footage, statements from eyewitnesses and other evidence. They said appropriate legal action would be taken following a proper investigation based on the evidence collected.

item.title: 5th Bay of Bengal Conversation begins in Dhaka Saturday
item.description:
The fifth edition of the international conference, the Bay of Bengal Conversation 2026, will begin in Dhaka on Saturday.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will inaugurate the three-day conference, which is being organised by the Centre for Governance Studies (CGS) at the Pan Pacific Sonargaon Dhaka.
The conference will bring together more than 200 speakers, over 300 delegates, and more than 1,000 participants from over 100 countries
Participants include former and present heads of state, ministers, diplomats, military experts, academics, researchers, journalists, business and investment leaders, human rights defenders, technology specialists, and representatives of international development organisations.
CGS President Zillur Rahman formally announced the commencement of the conference at a media exchange held at Pan Pacific Sonargaon on Friday morning.
“The Bay of Bengal is becoming increasingly important in the context of maritime security and regional geopolitics. As a vital link between South Asia and Southeast Asia, one of the key objectives of this initiative is to explore effective solutions to the challenges and opportunities rooted in the Bay,” he said.
Zillur said this year’s discussions will focus on geopolitics, security, trust, climate change, spirituality, and humanity.
He said CGS has already expanded its activities to the United States and plans to extend its presence to Brussels and Dubai in the future.

item.title: Saudi coalition accuses Houthis of drone attack on Medina
item.description:
Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis struck an electricity distribution station in the holy city of Medina in Saudi Arabia, the Saudi-led coalition said Thursday, sparking strong condemnation from the Muslim world.
The alleged attack came as fighting intensifies in Yemen, where government forces said they carried out attacks on Houthi targets and AFP journalists heard explosions in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.
The Saudi-led coalition said a drone struck Medina’s Taibah electricity distribution station, which provides power to the Prophet’s Mosque, as the Houthis denied involvement.
Medina, the burial place of the Prophet Mohammed and home to the Prophet’s Mosque, is one of Islam’s holiest cities alongside Mecca.
Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said a drone struck the Taibah electricity distribution station at 5:11am (0211 GMT) on September 29.
“The investigation and evidence gathered by the competent authorities have confirmed the involvement of the Terrorist Houthi Militia in planning and executing this cowardly terrorist act, based on after-action review and the wreckage of the drone used,” he said in a statement.
The coalition said one transformer was taken out of service without affecting the wider electricity network. Al-Maliki said the facility supplied electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque.
“This cowardly terrorist act, targeting a civilian facility providing electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque in Madinah, is a continuation of this extremist militia’s attempts to target the Two Holy Mosques,” he said.
The accusation came as fighting intensified in Yemen.
AFP correspondents heard loud explosions in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa on Thursday evening, while the internationally recognized government’s military said it had carried out strikes on Houthi targets in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz.
A spokesman said the military had conducted a “high-value targeting operation” in Sanaa and struck 11 targets in Saada.
He added that 27 air strikes had targeted an “integrated military system” belonging to the Houthis in Taiz.
The Houthis, who control Sanaa and much of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, have repeatedly launched drones and missiles at Saudi Arabia since the kingdom intervened in Yemen’s civil war in 2015.
Attacks linked to Islam’s holy cities, however, are rare.
On Thursday, a senior Houthi official again rejected accusations that the movement had targeted Islamic holy sites, according to Houthi media.
Turkey strongly condemned the alleged attack and voiced support for Saudi Arabia.
“We strongly condemn the Houthis’ attack on civilian infrastructure” in Medina, the foreign ministry said.
“These provocative attacks, which threaten Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and security and target the sacred values of the Islamic world, must cease immediately and unconditionally.”
Turkey said it reiterated its “strong support for Saudi Arabia” and called for steps to prevent further escalation.
Qatar also condemned the attack. In a statement, Doha said it was “a grave assault on the sanctity of Islamic holy sites,” a violation of Saudi sovereignty and international law.
It reaffirmed its “full solidarity” with Riyadh and said the kingdom’s security was an integral part of Gulf security.
The League of Arab States joined the chorus, calling the attack “an unacceptable transgression.”
The organization said the attack “provokes the sentiments of Muslims worldwide” and represented a dangerous escalation.
Al-Azhar, the Cairo-based institute of Sunni Islamic learning, also denounced the incident.
It said “targeting Medina provokes the sentiments of Muslims worldwide.”

MID: 162 journalists face attacks, threats, harassment in three months
item.description:
At least 162 journalists across the country faced attacks, threats, harassment and legal harassment in 112 separate incidents over the past three months while performing their professional duties, according to a monitoring report by private research organisation Media Initiative for Development (MID).
The report, released on Friday, said August recorded the highest number of incidents involving violence and harassment against journalists during the three-month period.
In July, 50 journalists were affected in 39 incidents across the country. The number rose to 44 incidents in August, affecting 67 journalists, a 12.8% increase from the previous month.
The situation improved somewhat in September, with 45 journalists affected in 29 incidents. Compared to August, the number of incidents fell by 34.1%, while the number of affected journalists declined by 32.8%.
The MID report said physical attacks and death threats were the main forms of intimidation used against journalists during the period. In July, death threats accounted for 48.7% of reported incidents, while physical attacks made up 28.2%.
The three-month period also saw serious incidents involving shootings, attacks on journalists’ homes and offices, the filing of cases and abductions.
Physical attacks increased sharply in August, accounting for 63.6% of all incidents. In September, physical attacks and threats each accounted for 37.9% of the incidents.
A media-wise analysis showed that journalists working for print media, particularly those in the field and outside major cities, were the most affected. Of the 162 journalists targeted during the period, 89 were reporters for daily newspapers, while 53 worked for television channels and 20 for online news outlets.
Geographically, attacks and harassment against journalists were reported in more than 30 districts. Dhaka, Chittagong, Sirajganj, Barisal and Sylhet divisions recorded comparatively higher numbers of incidents.
The MID also expressed concern over the limited legal action taken following attacks and threats against journalists.
According to the report, general diaries (GDs) were filed in 46.2% of incidents in July and 54.5% in August, while the rate of formal case filing remained very low. In September, no legal action was taken in at least 41.4% of the reported incidents.
On media freedom and journalists’ safety, MID Executive Director Rashedul Hasan said: “Violence against journalists is a direct attack on press freedom and people’s right to information.
The government must sincerely ensure journalists’ safety by conducting impartial and swift investigations into every incident and ensuring exemplary punishment for those responsible.”

Saudi plans Houthi offensive with 100,000 Yemeni troops, US, other countries' support
item.description:
IRAN-CRISIS/YEMEN

Saudi Arabia is planning an offensive against Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen, with options being considered including a coastal push to secure the Red Sea shipping route or an assault on multiple fronts, regional and Western officials told Reuters.

The operation, expected to be launched in the coming weeks, will by led by Yemeni forces on the ground, which are overseen by Riyadh, and supported by Saudi air strikes, according to six people with knowledge of the preparations.

While the US is already providing intelligence to support Riyadh's operations in Yemen, and some regional and European nations are providing mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom, the Saudi allies aren't expected to play a direct role in combat operations, said the people who requested anonymity to discuss security matters.

Saudi Arabia entered neighbouring Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition in support of the internationally recognised government, which the Houthis had driven out of the capital Sanaa. A truce agreed between the warring parties in 2022 largely held until this year when the Houthis launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure in a spillover from the Iran war.

A key objective of the planned Saudi offensive, which hasn't been previously reported, is aimed at reversing the rapid gains made by the Houthis last month when they advanced down the coast and seized control of the Bab el-Mandeb strait, according to the people with knowledge of the plans who include Gulf and Yemeni officials and Western diplomats.

The Saudis are considering two possible options for the assault, the Gulf and Yemeni officials said: Either a narrowly focused attack on the area around Bab el-Mandeb or a broader offensive that also includes other synchronized attacks on multiple fronts around Yemen, in the governorates of Al-Bayda, Marib, Taiz and Al-Jawf.

More than 100,000 Yemeni troops could be mobilized in the offensive, depending on the scale, the officials all said.

Spokespeople for the Saudi and Yemeni governments, the Houthi group and the US military didn't immediately respond to requests for comment about the Saudi plans.

Bab el-Mandeb is the southern exit passage of the Red Sea, a key shipping route between the Mediterranean and Asia that's assumed even more importance this year as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed by the Iran conflict.

Riyadh has concluded it cannot enter new Yemeni peace negotiations with the Houthis while the militants remain in control of Bab el-Mandeb, giving them significant global leverage, the Western diplomats and Gulf official said.

The six people with knowledge of the Saudi preparations couldn't give a precise timing for the launch of the offensive, with their estimates ranging from within a week to until after the US midterm elections in early November.

Michael Ratney, a former US ambassador to Saudi Arabia, said he expected an offensive to be narrowly focused and certainly more modest in scope than the Saudi-led operation in 2015 that sought to rout the militants.

"As much they want to vanquish the Houthis completely, they also need to get back to status quo ante before Houthis controlled territory along Bab el-Mandeb," he added. "Ideally, it would be a fairly limited operation to retake coastal areas and get back to normal maritime traffic."

The Houthis have become Iran's most formidable ally in the Middle East since Israel's degradation of Hezbollah in Lebanon over the past three years.

A Saudi-directed offensive against the group would mark a new flashpoint in a region engulfed by conflict since the Hamas-led attacks on Israel of 7 October 2023 and the subsequent US-Israeli war on Iran.

Trump, Turkey and Pakistan

Washington, Saudi Arabia's most powerful ally, is providing military advisers and intelligence including targeting information to support Saudi air operations in Yemen, according to one of the Western diplomats.

However, the extent of support may be limited. Reuters has previously reported that US President Donald Trump rebuffed requests by the de facto Saudi ruler Mohammed bin Salman for direct military support such as air strikes.

Turkey and Pakistan, with whom Saudi Arabia signed a joint defence agreement last month, have provided military equipment that the kingdom is using in Yemen, Pakistani and regional officials said.

Last month, Pakistan sent four cargo planes with equipment including air defence systems, light artillery, drones and anti-drone systems to Aden, the seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, a Pakistani government official said.

Pakistani military advisers are also on the ground with Saudi counterparts to support Yemeni forces, according to a second Pakistani official, the Gulf official and a Western diplomat. Turkish drones, bought by Saudi Arabia before the current war, have also been deployed over Yemen, they added.

One of the kingdom's key concerns in launching a new offensive in Yemen is how to protect its oil facilities and other infrastructure from Houthi drone and missile attacks, according to regional officials who said Riyadh has asked several allies for help with defensive systems.

Pakistan has deployed between 30,000 and 40,000 troops to Saudi Arabia to help defend the kingdom's land borders and help with drone and missile interceptions, according to the second Pakistani official, who said the troops arrived in waves beginning last year but also after the recent escalation. Islamabad hasn't made any decision to send troops into Yemen in a fighting capacity, the official said.

The Pakistani and Turkish defence ministries didn't respond to requests for comment on their military support for Riyadh.

France, meanwhile, has announced it will send defensive systems and troops to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu.

Fractured Yemeni forces

Any ground operation inside Yemen will rely on the disparate coalition of Yemeni fighting factions that Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates armed and trained at earlier stages of the civil war when the conflict ground to a bloody stalemate.

"Many anti-Houthi forces are still not organised or prepared for the kind of sustained offensive required to push back a disciplined Houthi military force. And they are being tested right now, as the Houthis apply pressure across several fronts at once," said Yemen analyst Mohammed Albasha.

Yemeni forces were further fractured last winter when southern fighters backed by the UAE tried to take territory in the east and announce secession plans, leading to their defeat by Saudi-backed fighters after a series of clashes.

Ali Shihabi, a Saudi political analyst close to government thinking, cautioned the outcome of any offensive by the Saudis against the Houthis would depend on how ground forces perform.

"The priority so far has been to defend the positions on the ground and stabilize the front, but certainly they will be going on the offensive," he said. "Success greatly depends on the quality of the performance of the local forces."

PM Tarique inaugurates fifth Bay of Bengal Conversation
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday inaugurated the fifth edition of the international forum "Bay of Bengal Conversation 2026", bringing together policymakers, diplomats, researchers and experts from over 100 countries.
The three-day conference, organised by the Centre for Governance Studies (CGS), is being held at the Pan Pacific Sonargaon Dhaka from October 3 to 5.
The prime minister formally opened the three-day event around 10am with his address to the opening session.
More than 200 speakers, over 300 delegates and more than 1,000 participants are expected to attend the forum, including former and current heads of state and government, ministers, diplomats, military experts, academics, researchers, journalists, business and investment leaders, human rights defenders, technology specialists and representatives of international development organisations.
Former Serbian President Boris Tadić and former Malian Prime Minister Moussa Mara are among the notable participants.
The theme of this year’s conference is “Fragments, Frontiers and Futures”, with the tagline “Navigating Power, Technology and Trust in a World Rewritten.”
The discussions will focus on major regional and global issues, including geopolitics and security, technology, trade and connectivity, climate change, human security, democracy, governance, trust, spirituality and humanity.
CGS President Zillur Rahman and Executive Director Parvez Karim Abbasi delivered the welcome remarks at the opening of the conference.
Zillur Rahman said the Bay of Bengal is becoming increasingly important in the context of maritime security and regional geopolitics.
“As a vital link between South Asia and Southeast Asia, one of the key objectives of this initiative is to explore effective solutions to the challenges and opportunities rooted in the Bay,” he said.
He said this year’s discussions would focus on geopolitics, security, trust, climate change, spirituality and humanity.
The program includes public sessions such as plenaries, leadership forums and spotlight talks, as well as smaller invitation-only roundtables for in-depth discussions, according to the organisers.

item.title: UK maritime agency: Oil tankers attacked in Hormuz strait
item.description:
Two oil tankers have been struck by "unidentified projectiles" in the Strait of Hormuz region, a British maritime agency said Friday, in the latest threat to shipping in the waterway.
The Hormuz passage, through which a fifth of the world's oil and LNG passed before the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in late February and sparked the Middle East war, remains at the heart of the conflict.
Tehran has been blocking the passage of commercial ships, firing on vessels it accuses of unauthorised crossings.
Washington responded with a counterblockade of Iranian ports in an effort to prevent Tehran from exporting its oil.
The first attack caused "a small fire and blackout onboard", the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said Friday, adding that the fire was later extinguished.
There were no reported casualties or environmental impact, it added.
The vessel, which was exiting the strait, was able to resume its journey, UKMTO said, without specifying the ship's ports of origin and destination.
Hours later, another crude oil tanker reported being struck by an "unknown projectile" east of Oman, with all crew safe and no environmental damage reported, according to the UKMTO.
The agency said authorities were investigating the incidents.

item.title: Uranium consignment reaches Rooppur nuclear power plant amid tight security
item.description:
A uranium consignment for the second unit of Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant reached the project site in Pabna on Saturday afternoon amid tight security.
Three uranium-laden lorries arrived at the nuclear power plant site around 12:25pm after leaving Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at around 7:15am under the security escort of the Bangladesh Army, said Pabna Deputy Commissioner Aminul Islam.
The consignment is the first shipment of uranium for the second unit of the Rooppur plant.
A special cargo aircraft carrying the uranium landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at around 11:44pm on Friday.
After completing the necessary formalities, the uranium was transported to Rooppur in three lorries while another vehicle carried other equipment.
A team of specialists who had arrived from Russia also accompanied the consignment.
Members of the Bangladesh Army, police and various intelligence agencies were deployed to ensure security during the transportation.
The flight carrying uranium for Rooppur plant was scheduled to arrive on September 24 but was not given permission to use Pakistani airspace.
According to project officials, a total of nine uranium consignments are scheduled to be brought to Bangladesh — seven for the second unit and two for the refuelling of the first unit.
All the consignments are scheduled to be delivered by December.
Fuel for the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant was brought to Bangladesh in 2023.
The Rooppur plant, comprising two 1,200-megawatt units, has a total generation capacity of 2,400MW.
Construction of the plant began in 2013 with Russian assistance at an estimated cost of more than Tk1.13 lakh crore.
Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Ltd (NPCBL) Managing Director Dr Zahidul Hasan said testing of the 16-megawatt high-pressure system under the reactor protection and safety-related system was successfully completed on Wednesday following the replacement of a defective valve.

item.title: With Russia next door and rising costs, Latvia goes to the polls
item.description:
Latvia will vote Saturday in an election shaped by concerns over neighboring Russia and the cost of living, but the result is not expected to steer the country off its pro-European and pro-Ukrainian course.
The center-right United List party of incumbent Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs is at the head of the race, with over 14% of the vote, according to the SKDS institute.
His coalition, however, is expected to emerge weakened as populist parties gain ground by focusing on economic concerns in the least affluent of the three Baltic states.
The current governing coalition is made up of United List, New Unity, the Union of Greens and Farmers, and the National Alliance. Polls suggest the bloc is unlikely to retain power in its current form after the vote.
Criticized as pro-Russian by its detractors, the populist Sovereign Power party, led by Julija Stepanenko, is polling at over nine percent and could become the second-largest party in Latvia’s 100-seat unicameral parliament.
The party has opposed military aid to Ukraine and further increases to defense spending, instead highlighting domestic economic problems.
Despite its gains, the party is unlikely to enter government because most major parties have ruled out cooperation with it.
Another populist force, Latvia First, led by businessman Ainars Slesers, could prove a more viable coalition partner.
The Progressives, a pro-European social democratic party advocating stronger social protections and continued support for Ukraine, are polling around six percent.
With roughly one in five voters still undecided, the final composition of the next parliament remains uncertain. Fourteen electoral lists are contesting the election, but polls indicate only seven are likely to clear the 5% threshold needed to enter parliament.
Security remains central to political debate four years after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
Latvia, a member of Nato and the European Union since 2004, views Russia as its principal security threat and has significantly increased defense spending in response.
It has sharply increased its defense spending since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Kyiv, now allocating nearly five percent of its GDP to defense.
Most parties expected to enter parliament support maintaining military spending at elevated levels and continuing assistance to Kyiv.
Economic issues nevertheless remain crucial to voters. Rising living costs, low wages, strains on the healthcare system and long-term population decline all feature prominently in campaign debates.
Voting patterns among Latvia’s large Russian-speaking minority are also changing.
Once concentrated behind the Harmony party, which lost parliamentary representation in 2022, many voters are increasingly making choices based on economic and social issues rather than identity politics alone.
Once ballots are counted, attention is likely to shift quickly to coalition negotiations, which could prove lengthy and complex.
Partial results are expected on Saturday evening, with preliminary official results due on Sunday.
Exit polls are expected shortly after polling stations close.

item.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile after Seoul’s apology demand
item.description:
North Korea fired a ballistic missile, Seoul’s military said Saturday, days after demanding an apology for a blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the DMZ that it blames on the North.
Pyongyang has denied responsibility for last month’s explosion inside the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) and called South Korea “despicable” on Friday, undercutting overtures by Seoul’s civilian leadership seeking a return to dialogue.
Early Saturday, “our military detected a ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area of North Korea toward the East Sea,” Seoul’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said, referring to the body of water also known as the Sea of Japan.
“South Korea, the US, and Japan are maintaining a robust defense posture through close information sharing regarding North Korean ballistic missiles,” it said, adding the missile flew more than 700 kilometers (435 miles).
Seoul and the US-led United Nations Command found that last month’s explosion inside the DMZ, the heavily mined buffer dividing the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice, was caused by North Korean mines laid on the South side of the border.
North Korea’s military has laid mines and built anti-tank barriers along the frontier as part of efforts to permanently seal it off following leader Kim Jong Un’s designation of South Korea as his country’s “principal enemy” in 2024.
The mines responsible for the blast, which left three soldiers wounded, were believed to have been laid as part of Pyongyang’s border fortification work, according to South Korea’s defense minister Kang Shin-chul.
South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung had urged Pyongyang on Thursday to return to dialogue, despite his military demanding an apology a day earlier.
Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea’s leader, responded by calling Seoul “really despicable” on Friday and once again denied Pyongyang was behind the blasts.
She ridiculed Lee’s latest overture, calling it “the climax of the farce that everyone should watch” and said the military’s demand her country apologize was “quite ridiculous.”
Kim also warned Pyongyang was “ready for anything” Seoul might do over the mine blast -- remarks followed the next morning by North Korea’s ballistic missile launch.
Analysts said the launch would be viewed as a show of force in response to the South Korean government’s diplomatic efforts, effectively rejecting engagement.
“Seoul called for easing tensions, but Pyongyang answered by escalating them,” Yang Moo-jin, former president of the University of North Korean Studies in Seoul, told AFP.
“The message is that the North is pursuing... confrontation in response to goodwill,” he added.
South Korea’s defense minister said on Tuesday the military had “a range of necessary measures at our disposal, and we will implement them in stages” to respond to the DMZ incident, without providing further detail.
The South’s Unification Minister, Chung Dong-young, also proposed talks to address issues along the border to Pyongyang on Friday.
Kim Yo Jong, however, dismissed Chung’s suggestion of talks as a “wild dream and unilateral jargon.”
The flare-up comes at a sensitive time when US President Donald Trump’s recent overtures to Pyongyang have raised concerns that Seoul -- an ally of Washington -- could be sidelined in potential nuclear talks involving the North.
South Korea’s opposition People Power Party on Friday accused Lee of failing to criticize Pyongyang when warranted even as he takes a hard line on Ukraine for publicly disclosing the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war, an arrangement Seoul believed should be confidential.
“South Korean soldiers have been injured, and far from receiving an apology, we have been mocked by North Korea,” the opposition party said in a statement.
“We fail to see how selectively turning a blind eye to North Korea serves South Korea’s dignity or the safety of its people.”
